title: How to Use the 1-Minute Preparation Time
answer_framework:
The 1-minute preparation time in Part 2 is crucial. Do NOT try to write full sentences—you will run out of time and end up reading from your notes, which ruins your Fluency and Pronunciation scores. Instead, use the 'Keyword & Map' method:

1. Read the card quickly (10 seconds) and decide on a topic immediately. Do not change your mind halfway through.
2. Write down 1-2 keywords for each bullet point (30 seconds). Focus on high-level vocabulary, idioms, or specific adjectives you want to force yourself to use.
3. Note down the tenses (20 seconds). Quickly scribble 'Past -> Present -> Future' on your paper to remind yourself to shift tenses for a better Grammar score.
useful_phrase_bank: Well, when I first saw this topic, I immediately thought of... (Opening)
As for why it was so significant... (Transition to final bullet)

weak_vs_better.weak_answer: (Looking at notes) I... went... to... the beach. It... was... sunny.
weak_vs_better.better_answer: (Glancing at notes for a keyword like 'scorching') When I visited the beach, the weather was absolutely scorching, which made the ocean feel incredibly refreshing.

fluency_pronunciation_note: Your notes are just a map. Glance at them, then make eye contact with the examiner while you speak the sentence. This natural eye contact helps maintain a conversational, fluent rhythm.
sample_ielts_question:
Describe an important decision you made.
- What it was
- How you made it
- Who helped you
- And explain why it was important.
model_short_answer: When I saw this card, I immediately thought of my decision to study abroad. During my prep time, I wrote down 'daunting', 'consulted', and 'turning point'. It was a daunting choice because I'd never lived alone. I consulted my older sister, who had studied in Australia. Ultimately, it was a turning point because it made me entirely self-sufficient.
common_mistakes: Writing full sentences during the 1 minute.
Staring at the paper the entire time while speaking.
Wasting 30 seconds trying to choose the 'perfect' story.
image_prompt_fallback: A close-up of a person's hand quickly jotting down bullet points and keywords on a small notepad with a pen, under a soft desk light.

quiz.question: What should you primarily write down during your 1-minute prep time?

options.A: Full sentences so you don't forget your grammar.
options.B: Only the first sentence of your story.
options.C: Keywords, high-level vocabulary, and tense reminders.

quiz.explanation: Writing keywords and vocabulary forces you to speak naturally (Fluency) while ensuring you hit your target words (Lexical Resource). Full sentences lead to robotic reading.
